subject: Adaptation Fails in RStan 2.1.0, but Functions OK in RStan 2.0.1

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: Adaptation Fails in RStan 2.1.0, but Functions OK in RStan 2.0.1
parts:
Immediately after Stan 2.0.1 was released I built up an adaptive phylogenetic evolution model, following a paper by Butler and King. The Butler and King model relies on having a known phylogenetic tree with branch lengths (cut times between sucessive nodes). I wrote some code to integrate over uncertainty in the size of these branch lengths, +/- 350 years. Each newly proposed tree was checked for internal consistency (no child node older than a parent) using Stan's positive_ordered vecotor type. The modeled appeared to function well, recovering parameters on constructed data.

I updated RStan upon receiving an email suggesting I rerun anything run under Stan 2.0.1, as there was a bug in the code.

In RStan 2.1.0 adaptation fails, in that at every iteration a proposed positive_ordered vector violates constraints and is rejected (that happens with up to 5,000 iters of warmup).

Is there any way I can reset Rstan 2.1.0 to have the exact same warm up specs as Rstan 2.0.1? If not, is the bug in Stan 2.0.1 bad enough that samples from a non-hierarchical model would  be too biased to warrant publication?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Adaptation Fails in RStan 2.1.0, but Functions OK in RStan 2.0.1

On 1/10/14, 6:51 AM, Cody Ross wrote:
> Immediately after Stan 2.0.1 was released I built up an adaptive phylogenetic evolution model, following a paper by
> Butler and King. The Butler and King model relies on having a known phylogenetic tree with branch lengths (cut times
> between sucessive nodes). I wrote some code to integrate over uncertainty in the size of these branch lengths, +/- 350
> years. Each newly proposed tree was checked for internal consistency (no child node older than a parent) using Stan's
> positive_ordered vecotor type. The modeled appeared to function well, recovering parameters on constructed data.
Glad to hear it.

> I updated RStan upon receiving an email suggesting I rerun anything run under Stan 2.0.1, as there was a bug in the code.
>
> In RStan 2.1.0 adaptation fails, in that at every iteration a proposed positive_ordered vector violates constraints and
> is rejected (that happens with up to 5,000 iters of warmup).

As part of the 2.1.0 release, we fixed another bug that caused
step size to be initialized from init=0 rather than from the
user-specified init or random inits. It's not possible to recreate
the 2.0.1 behavior exactly because it was a bug in the way init was
being done.

If the model worked in 2.0.1, it should work in 2.1.0 with init=0.
This also sets the initial parameter values to 0 on the unconstrained
scale.

But if it only works with init=0 and not other inits, then
there may be a problem in the model specification. If the positive_ordered
vector is a parameter, the only way it should be able to violate constraints
would be due to overflow or underflow.

> Is there any way I can reset Rstan 2.1.0 to have the exact same warm up specs as Rstan 2.0.1? If not, is the bug in Stan
> 2.0.1 bad enough that samples from a non-hierarchical model would be too biased to warrant publication?

I'll leave that one for Andrew --- he's the one who found the bug.

- Bob

>> 2.0.1 bad enough that samples from a non-hierarchical model would be too biased to warrant publication?

I think Bob is saying we can have the same inits by setting init=0, so it makes sense to try that first. Otherwise, if all you have are the Stan 2.0.1 runs, you have a couple options. One option is to take them as is. I don't think the inferences are _too_ horrible; in the bivaraiate normal case, we were getting a sd of 0.96 instead of 1.0, and according to Mike B., the bivariate case happens to be the worst case of that bug. Another option would be to take the draws from the Stan 2.0.1 runs, consider them as a correct summary of the posterior distribution, and do some posterior predictive checks. But really I wouldn't feel so comfortable until it's running in 2.1--I agree with Bob that it sounds like there could be a problem with the model (Bob is invoking the Folk Theorem here, I believe).

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: Re: Adaptation Fails in RStan 2.1.0, but Functions OK in RStan 2.0.1
parts:
I used init=0 in both 2.0.1, and 2.1.0. The model specification might be the problem, but it woud be weird that it run fines in one Rstan version and not the other.

The positive_ordered vector is a transformed parameter. It is a the sum of  the MLE values of linguistic divergence dates plus or minus some random deviation. It is the case that introducing uncertainty this way can lead to proposals in which child nodes are older than parent nodes. I was using positive_ordered as a check, to ensure than any such proposals were rejected. 

I'll go back and check to make sure support is matching declarations.

The sensitivity analysis I ran with the model using simulated data was decently thorough - the model recovered appropriate parameters in each of 10 cases of simulated data, and WAIC preferred the more complex model only when simulated data were created using a model in which adaptive evolution depended on the ecological regime investigated with the more complex model.

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: Re: Adaptation Fails in RStan 2.1.0, but Functions OK in RStan 2.0.1
parts:
What email address should I send the model/data to?

I originally had this model running in RStan since it allows me to save only some of the parameters as samples using pars=c(lorum, ipsum, etc.) (is this possible in CmdStan too?)

I just ran the model in CmdStan, and noticed the same phenomenon, of incessant "the current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected" warnings during warm up and sampling; however, when I took a look at the traceplot, the model appears to function fine, moving into the correct (according to the simulated data) posterior region, and mixing.

What is notable is that the tree depth is low, max=3, sometimes = -1 .

What exactly triggers the "the current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected" warnings?

 At first, I had thought that the warning was only thrown when the proposed parameter state got rejected after failing to pass a constraint check. Ie. the sample after rejecting a parameter state at iteration X, is identical to the parameter state at X-1. From the last run of this model, it looks the simulation at a given iteration X might attempt to go out to 4 steps, for example, but at step 4 violate a constraint, this triggers the warning; however, the exported parameter state (the sample) is the parameter state at step 3 of iteration X, rather than previous iteration's (X-1) parameter state.

Looking at the Cmd prompt, a warning was issued for every warm-up sample from sample to sample 200. However, after saving warm-up and looking at the samples, only the first 3 proposals and about 3 others spread over the next 190 samples were actually rejected.

Could it just be that Stan 2.1.0 is more generous than Stan 2.0.1 about when it throws the "the current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected" warnings?

On 1/14/14, 6:40 AM, Cody Ross wrote:
> What email address should I send the model/data to?
You can send to me: ca...@alias-i.com

> I originally had this model running in RStan since it allows me to save only some of the parameters as samples using
> pars=c(lorum, ipsum, etc.) (is this possible in CmdStan too?)
>
> I just ran the model in CmdStan, and noticed the same phenomenon, of incessant "the current Metropolis proposal is about
> to be rejected" warnings during warm up and sampling; however, when I took a look at the traceplot, the model appears to
> function fine, moving into the correct (according to the simulated data) posterior region, and mixing.
>
> What is notable is that the tree depth is low, max=3, sometimes = -1 .
That's fine depending on the model. Some models only need tree depth of 1.

> What exactly triggers the "the current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected" warnings?


> At first, I had thought that the warning was only thrown when the proposed parameter state got rejected after failing
> to pass a constraint check.

That's correct. But we do multiple proposals along the path
of the simulated Hamiltonian.

> Ie. the sample after rejecting a parameter state at iteration X, is identical to the
> parameter state at X-1.

Not quite. We can still sample if we move and then get into
a bad space.

The cause is almost always one of arithmetic underflow, overflow or
parameters defined without the proper constraints so that the support
of the probability function defined in the model doesn't match the
constraints.

> From the last run of this model, it looks the simulation at a given iteration X might attempt to
> go out to 4 steps, for example, but at step 4 violate a constraint, this triggers the warning; however, the exported
> parameter state (the sample) is the parameter state at step 3 of iteration X, rather than previous iteration's (X-1)
> parameter state.
Right --- the -1 is the only time the first step gets rejected.

> Looking at the Cmd prompt, a warning was issued for every warm-up sample from sample to sample 200. However, after
> saving warm-up and looking at the samples, only the first 3 proposals and about 3 others spread over the next 190
> samples were actually rejected.
>
> Could it just be that Stan 2.1.0 is more generous than Stan 2.0.1 about when it throws the "the current Metropolis
> proposal is about to be rejected" warnings?

It's not more generous on error checking, but it tries to adapt to a
smaller step size with more rejections due to the plain-old Metropolis/slice
condition. One of the reasons we made this change is that it's more
robust. So if you're in an area of high curvature, a big step (which is
a linear approximation of the posterior based on the gradient) can be
rejected whereas two smaller steps won't be rejected.

- Bob
